title: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0
body_markdown:
Today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced version 1.0 of ExtendDB, the first release of the open source Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter for production use. ExtendDB is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and runs on a database backend that you choose, so developers and infrastructure teams can run DynamoDB workloads in on-premises data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge without rewriting application code.


ExtendDB 1.0 supports four storage backends, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB. For local development and continuous integration (CI), the[extenddb-dev container image](https://hub.docker.com/r/extenddb/extenddb-dev) and the[@extenddb/dev npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@extenddb/dev) package run a DynamoDB-compatible endpoint over SQLite, so you don’t have to set up an external database.


ExtendDB is maintained by AWS, released under the Apache 2.0 license, and developed in the open on GitHub. To learn more, see the[ExtendDB project page](https://extenddb.org/) . To get started or contribute, visit the[GitHub repository](https://github.com/ExtendDB/extenddb) .
